rule_checks.verbatim_excerpt: (7) For installation of roof top solar photo voltaic systems, the technical feasibility study shall be completed within a period of fifteen days and the outcome of the study shall be intimated to the applicant, failing which it shall be presumed that the proposal is technically feasible. (7A) The applications for roof top solar photo voltaic systems upto 10 kW capacity, complete in all respects shall be deemed to have been accepted without requiring technical feasibility study and any commensurate enhancement of the sanctioned load of the consumer, as may be required, shall be carried out by the distribution licensee.”;
rule_checks.notes: Substance of the claimed rule is stated (no feasibility study up to 10 kW; deemed accepted; licensee enhances sanctioned load) but NOT verbatim: real text says "deemed to have been accepted", no mention of "portal" or "conveying of technical feasibility shall be deemed". Real clause numbering is rule 11(7A) (and 11(7): 15-day study for all RTS with presumed feasibility), not rule 11(1)/(2). Excerpts are copied from the extracted text with line breaks collapsed to single spaces; " || " separates non-contiguous excerpts.

caveats: Claimed number G.S.R. 132(E) is wrong; gazette copy reads G.S.R. 125(E).

Spec edge evidence quote "in rule 11, for sub-rules (1) and (2), the following sub-rules shall be substituted" is FALSE: the real amendment substitutes rule 11 sub-rules (7), (8) and (9) and inserts (7A) and (9A).
Fabricated 11(2) "exceeding 10 kW ... fifteen days ... deemed approved": real 11(7) applies the 15-day/presumed-feasible rule to ALL rooftop solar installations, not only >10 kW.

Mirror: hosted on CEA (upadhi.cea.gov.in), an official GoI domain; it is the Government of India Press gazette print. powermin.gov.in URLs now 404 after site migration. Hindi half of the PDF has a garbled text layer; English half is clean.

rule_checks.verbatim_excerpt: 8.8 Within twenty (20) days from the issuance of acknowledgement of the application, the concerned officer of the respective Sub-divisional office of the Distribution Licensee shall check the technical feasibility of the Renewable Energy generating system. 8.9 If technical feasibility is found satisfactory, the Distribution Licensee shall approve the application and intimate the same to the applicant by providing a Letter of Approval (LoA) via email/SMS/post, within thirty (30) days from the issuance of acknowledgement of the application. || [p.100] 7.2 The maximum Renewable Energy generating system capacity to be installed at any Eligible Consumer’s premises shall not exceed 100% of the Sanctioned Load/Contract Demand of the consumer:
rule_checks.substitute_doc_id_or_url: RJ-C3-002 (RERC DREGS Regulations 2021, already in corpus: regs 7.2, 8.8, 8.9); also Annexure-IV of this JVVNL order
rule_checks.notes: Claimed JVVNL order "JPR5-1022" dated 15.09.2022 was NOT found. The rule is substantially stated in the RERC 2021 Regulations (enclosed by this authentic JVVNL 2022 order): feasibility check within 20 days and LoA within 30 days of acknowledgement; capacity not to exceed 100% of Sanctioned Load/Contract Demand. Differences: real cap is on SANCTIONED load (not "connected load"); 30 days runs from acknowledgement, with deficiencies notified within 20 working days (reg 8.10) rather than a "formal rejection within 30 days"; no "physical site inspection within 15 days by JEN" rule. Excerpts are copied from the extracted text with line breaks collapsed to single spaces; " || " separates non-contiguous excerpts.

caveats: The JVVNL cover order itself is about vendor empanelment; it states the rule only through its enclosed RERC regulations. The primary rule source is RJ-C3-002.
